previous_text: When a vendor in good standing has a recently expired ISO 9001 certificate, the procurement exception should be resolved by applying step codes REQUEST_RENEWED_CERT, KEEP_VENDOR_ACTIVE, and HOLD_PO rather than immediate rejection, as demonstrated in case PR-2026-0417.

source_facts.text: Procurement case PR-2026-0417 for ₹1,40,000 worth of bearing housings from vendor V-017 was blocked due to an expired ISO 9001 certificate. | When: 2026-03-14 | Involving: R. Menon (Procurement Ops), V-017 (vendor) | The standard vendor check blocks vendors with expired certifications, but V-017 had a 2-year history of on-time delivery and was in the process of renewing.
R. Menon approved step codes REQUEST_RENEWED_CERT, KEEP_VENDOR_ACTIVE, and HOLD_PO to resolve the procurement exception. | When: 2026-03-14 | Involving: R. Menon (Procurement Ops)
The vendor provided a renewed certificate within 3 days, allowing the purchase order to be released. | When: 2026-03-17 | Involving: V-017 (vendor)
A recently expired certificate should be treated as a hold rather than a rejection when the vendor is in good standing. | Lesson learned from case PR-2026-0417.
